principles: A Desktop AI chat/session is disposable; repository state is durable.
An independent lightweight watchdog checks session health even if the main unified scheduler or Desktop AI UI is blocked.
Watchdog states include LIVE, WAITING_VALID, ACTION_REQUIRED, SCHEDULER_OVERDUE, AUTO_RECOVERING, STALLED, DEAD, ESCALATION_REQUIRED, and IDLE.
WAITING_VALID is not a hang: known long-soak/timer-managed work may legitimately show no frequent changes.
STALLED means a responsible PID is alive but no durable progress was observed beyond the configured threshold; diagnose before killing.
DEAD means unfinished work exists but the responsible process is proven absent/dead; create a recovery checkpoint and continue in a fresh session.
Every resume scans durable state plus live OS processes before suggesting the next action.
A still-running background process must never be started a second time merely because the chat session restarted.
An interrupted command is neither PASS nor FAIL until its side effects and evidence are reconciled.
Git reality wins over stale recovery metadata.
Timer-managed waiting work remains visible across sessions and is not converted to fake PASS.
Never clear a live lock, never fabricate evidence, never auto-commit/push/merge from the recovery engine.
LIVE is forbidden when required blocking work exists, no worker is active, and the action-required grace has expired.
An overdue durable timer is SCHEDULER_OVERDUE, never LIVE; the watchdog may safely kick blockers:tick through the existing unified lock.
When ACTION_REQUIRED persists and no worker exists, the watchdog may launch one non-interactive OpenCode recovery worker if the CLI is available.
Automatic OpenCode recovery must read repository recovery state first, never duplicate live work, never fake PASS, never work directly on master, and never auto-merge master.
Automatic agent retries are bounded for an unchanged blocker fingerprint; repeated no-progress becomes ESCALATION_REQUIRED instead of an infinite token-consuming loop.
